title: Diffusion Denoising Loop
beginner_answer: Diffusion generation starts from noise and repeatedly predicts how to remove noise. Each step updates the noisy sample toward something more image-like.
operator_rule: More steps give the process more chances to refine, but extra steps do not guarantee better output forever.

title: Latent Space
beginner_answer: Latent space is a compressed working space. Stable Diffusion-style models usually denoise the compressed latent first, then decode it back into visible pixels.
operator_rule: Latent problems can become visible as color, detail, or identity artifacts after decoding.

title: Scheduler Route
beginner_answer: The scheduler controls the route through denoising timesteps. It decides how the model moves from noise toward the final output.
operator_rule: There is no universal best sampler or scheduler; it is model and task dependent.
failure_signatures: model looks weak with wrong scheduler

title: Tokenization
beginner_answer: A tokenizer converts text into numerical chunks the model can process. Models do not directly read English words.
operator_rule: One token is not always one word; spelling, punctuation, rare names, and long prompts can change behavior.

title: Attention
beginner_answer: Attention is a learned relevance calculation between pieces of input. It helps the model decide which pieces matter to each other.
operator_rule: Attention is not awareness; it is a computation pattern.

title: LoRA Adapter
beginner_answer: A LoRA is a small trainable adapter added to a frozen base model. It teaches a narrower behavior without retraining the whole model.
operator_rule: LoRA strength is steering strength, not a quality slider.

title: Training Ladder
beginner_answer: Prompting changes inference inputs; textual inversion changes an embedding; LoRA changes adapter weights; full fine-tuning changes much more of the model.
operator_rule: Use the smallest intervention that solves the problem before moving to heavier training.
failure_signatures: using training when workflow control would solve it

title: Overfitting
use_when: loss looks good but samples bad
beginner_answer: Overfitting means the model learned the training examples too narrowly instead of learning a flexible concept.
operator_rule: Validate with samples. Loss is an instrument panel, not a judge.

title: PEFT and QLoRA
beginner_answer: PEFT adapts a pretrained model by training a smaller set of extra parameters. QLoRA combines quantized base loading with LoRA-style adapter training to reduce memory use.
operator_rule: Quantization can make local adaptation possible, but hardware/backend details still matter.

title: ControlNet Structural Conditioning
beginner_answer: ControlNet adds an external structural guide to a pretrained diffusion model. The prompt says what; the control map helps say where and how.
operator_rule: ControlNet is structural conditioning, not the same as identity reference or an inpainting mask.

title: DiT and Newer Backbones
beginner_answer: Some newer diffusion models use transformer-style backbones or other modern generative approaches instead of the older U-Net Stable Diffusion recipe.
operator_rule: Do not blindly transfer SD 1.5 settings to every model family.
failure_signatures: old settings fail on new model
